messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: KV-cache error rate + continuous-batching latency surge detected in us-west-2 (svc: inference-runtime). Rolling 5m tail: error_rate=4.7% (norm 0.1%), p95 latency increased 3.2x. Pager sent to #incidents.
lee_oncall: acked. I'm on it. Pulling metrics and traces now.
maria_sre: on call handover — I'm standby and can grab infra tasks. lee, do you have a suspected root cause? any customer impact yet?
lee_oncall: early hypothesis: prefix/prompt cache invalidations have been spiking, causing mass cache misses and KV write amplification. That in turn triggers larger batches and some pathologically large token windows -> memory pressure + timeouts.
jordan_ops: seeing corresponding spike on KV write QPS on redis-kvpool-usw2-1: grafana -> https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/kv/kv-write-qps?orgId=1 panel=promptkey
sarah_eng: logs show a flood of PutPrefix calls with 4096-byte keys, many from the same templated prompt pattern. Search:

  HTTP  2026-03-15T14:02:02Z PUT /v1/kv/prefixkey 200  size=4096 model=xlarge prompt_hash=0x7f9a3
  HTTP  2026-03-15T14:02:03Z PUT /v1/kv/prefixkey 200  size=4096 model=xlarge prompt_hash=0x1a2b4

lee_oncall: interesting — tokenizer mismatch earlier this week bumped tokenize_normalize flag on a subset of hosts. Could be template drift + hash regen causing keys to change often.
maria_sre: customer-impact check: CS bot, any active customer incidents opened? cs-bot, can you look for inbound alerts / increases in support tickets?
cs-bot: Noted. 3 support tickets in the last 20m referencing timeouts and 2 alerts from enterprise-cust-57 (embed-generation timeout). No customer-facing outage recorded yet, but elevated error rate for some customers.
lee_oncall: mitigation plan (live):
- throttle KV writes for non-critical prefixes (set write_rate_limit=10req/s) on region us-west-2
- temporarily reduce continuous batching token limit on the runtime pool from 4096 -> 1024
- enable emergency KV sweep to evict stale promptkey fragments older than 5m
- notify customers via CS if we detect >30% impact to requests for a given org

jordan_ops: applying KV write throttle to redis-kvpool-usw2-1 now.

  # ops run
  curl -X POST "https://ops-api.internal/kv/ratelimit" -d '{"pool":"usw2-1","rate":10}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN'

jordan_ops: rate limit applied. Watching.
sarah_eng: prepping runtime hotfix: reduce max_batch_tokens. Pushing change to canary nodes first.

  # runtime config patch
  kubectl -n runtime apply -f - <<EOF
  apiVersion: v1
  kind: ConfigMap
  metadata:
    name: batch-config
  data:
    max_batch_tokens: "1024"
    batch_timeout_ms: "20"
  EOF

sarah_eng: canary updated. Observing p95 on canary dropping ~45% vs baseline.
lee_oncall: good. Roll to remainder of pool in 3 waves, 20% each.
maria_sre: starting KV sweep script to clear promptkey fragments older than 5m. Command:

  python tools/kv_sweep.py --pool usw2-1 --age 300 --dry-run

maria_sre: dry-run shows ~42k keys to sweep (most small fragments). Running live sweep now with 5 worker concurrency.
maria_sre: sweep running.

  INFO kv_sweep: deleted 1000 keys, 120s elapsed
  INFO kv_sweep: deleted 5000 keys, 600s elapsed

maria_sre: initial sweep reduced memory pressure and evictions went down. KV write QPS dropped ~60%.
cs-bot: Notifying CS reps for affected customers. Draft message queued for enterprise-cust-57 and a handful of SMB orgs: "We are investigating elevated timeouts affecting embeddings/generation in us-west-2; mitigation in progress. No confirmed data loss. Updates in #incidents."
lee_oncall: monitoring shows p95 latency back to ~1.2x baseline and error_rate down to 0.4%. Still above normal but much better.
sarah_eng: quick note — root cause likely multi-factor: tokenizer normalization toggle + template rollout caused frequent prompt rehashing, combined with a recent batch config increase in a canary which increased max_batch_tokens to 4096 (rolled last week). The combination produced large writes and eviction cascades.
jordan_ops: added temporary alert rule to block re-roll of batch config into prod: tag=block-rollout-3087654321
lee_oncall: summary for now: 1) KV write throttle applied; 2) batch tokens reduced to 1024; 3) KV sweep executed; 4) canary rollback guard set; 5) CS notified. Immediate customer risk mitigated.
maria_sre: can someone take ownership for a postmortem? Need timeline, contributing factors (tokenizer change + batch bump + template drift), and remediation (add deterministic prefix hashing + canary gating + KV TTL defaults + automated sweep on surge).
sarah_eng: I'll own the postmortem write-up and follow with a PR for deterministic hashing + hashing-integrity tests.
lee_oncall: handoff: I'm off in 30m. maria, can you keep watching for 2h and escalate to infra if error_rate spikes >1%?
maria_sre: yep will watch. I'll also coordinate with Sarah on the PR and schedule a follow-up deployment window.
cs-bot: CS update: enterprise-cust-57 reported intermittent timeouts for 15-20 minutes; we proactively offered a status note and ETA for root cause. No escalations yet.
lee_oncall: tagging action items for next oncall and eng teams:
- SRE: add KV surge detector and automated partial-sweep playbook (owner: maria_sre)
- Runtime: add canary gating for batch config changes + revert last week's global bump (owner: sarah_eng)
- Devex: add prompt hashing tests to CI to catch tokenizer drift (owner: jordan_ops)
- CS: follow up with affected customers and log any escalations (owner: cs-bot)

sarah_eng: will open revert PR and a smaller, controlled roll plan for batch tokens.
maria_sre: monitoring notes: keep alert thresholds slightly lower for 24h; set workspace-level throttles for customers who hit >50% error_rate.
lee_oncall: leaving a final note before going offcall: system stable for now, keep working handoff to next oncall (maria). Postmortem draft expected by EOD. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
maria_sre: acknowledged. taking over. ping if anything regresses.
cs-bot: Filed incident ticket INC-2026-0437 for tracking and CS comms.

lee_oncall: :white_check_mark: closing my loop. Good work team.
